Pass 1, 2026-09-19. Baseline `origin/main` at `bd643929a`. No card taken; CPU only. My first duty
was the proof protocol, not a dispatch, and writing it meant checking the charter's ground truth
against upstream. **Six of its stated facts did not survive that check**, one of which deletes a
deliverable from the campaign's central row.

PROTOCOL: `~/.coworker/state/of3t/PROTOCOL.md`, forty-three amendments. **Amended at pass 414: A43 — an angle may be read ONLY from a triple satisfying `rel^2 = 1 + r^2 - 2 r cos`, and the residual must be published beside it.** `of3t-angle` found the campaign carries TWO definitions of the same three aggregates: `score.py`'s mass-weighted triple mixes a QUADRATIC mean of rel with ARITHMETIC means of r and cos, so the identity fails on it by **25 %** on R149's own shipped arm. Every direction number this campaign publishes — 45.763°, 35.561°, 35.13° — is in the CONCATENATED definition and carries a residual between 1.1e-16 and 2.1e-15, audited this pass. An aggregate that fails the identity summarises error MAGNITUDE and carries no direction: quote its `rel`, never its `cos`.** **Amended at pass 382: A40's second half — a capture's WITNESS and its frame's GATING CONTROL test different things, and the control already existed.** `of3t-conditioning` built it two rows earlier, named it **COTANGENT_COMPLETE**, and wrote the principle down (`capture_cond_boundary.py:15-22`: *'a cotangent at a boundary is a complete gradient only if the parameters reach the loss through that boundary alone... an expectation is not a check'*). `capture_model_frame.py:232-234` shipped without it and argued the opposite in a comment: *'A boundary and a cotangent cannot be checked directly against anything.'* That sentence is false and it was load-bearing — it is why no successor asked. The witness passed at 1.7e-14 and was read as validating the frame; it asserts PROVENANCE and structurally cannot see a replay defect. **A frame with a green witness and no control is not a validated frame and reads exactly like one.** So D242 is a regression against this campaign's own established practice, not an oversight. **Pass 381: A40 — A FRAME'S GATING CONTROL IS A PRECONDITION OF THE FRAME, NOT A LATER CHECK ON IT.** No frame may grade anything until the control that says it is the frame it claims has RUN and PASSED. `of3t-modelframe` built the model frame, published the clause at 1.7814x from it, and the campaign spent three passes reasoning about that number; `of3t-twoside` ran the control two passes later and it fails by **twelve orders of magnitude** (D242). The control was cheap, it was specified in the brief, and it was owed at the point the first ratio was published. Its corollary: **a row that finds its own frame broken has delivered its result** — `of3t-twoside`'s STOP is worth more than the arm it was dispatched for. **Pass 380: A39** — A34's same-boundary requirement binds the DENOMINATOR too; no row may publish a ratio with an injected numerator and a full-model denominator without saying which side is injected and which way the bias runs (D241/R135). Its sibling: **an exclusion inherits its instrument's blind axis** — state the axis a falsifier reads and check the cause is not invariant along it before quoting it as settled (R136). History: `state/of3t/PASSLOG.md`.

**The four standing amendments a successor most needs**: A42 (a cotangent CORRECTION is part of the injected cotangent, so one correction,
one source, asserted by digest across a comparison), A41 (a multi-output cotangent injection
is valid only if the outputs are a graph cut), A40 (a frame's gating control is a precondition of
the frame), A37 (a projection is a PREDICTION, never a TARGET, and no bar may be derived from
one), A34 (both sides of a per-parameter comparison on the SAME boundary). PROTOCOL carries all
forty-one.

**The 20-step trajectory, on the SHIPPED default, at 88.0819 % of the model (pass 307,
`of3t-trajwide`, GO condition 3 — MET).** `rel_d` **2.564253e-01** at k = 20 with a log-log growth
exponent of **-0.27724** (intercept -0.46711, r2 0.9050) over the full **k = 2..20**, zero rungs
dropped, falling monotonically at every rung. **SUB-LINEAR, and §7b's bar is the shape**:
super-linear fails at any magnitude, and this is the opposite sign. **980 of 980** tape resolutions
at every step of every arm, so D126 does not recur at this scope; `d_1` exactly **0** on both
sides, which `lr(1) = 0` requires; **1752.90x** the fp32 differencing floor at k = 20 and never
under 19.20x from k = 2. The controls separate rather than agreeing quietly: the A16 `zero` model
reads exactly **1.000000e+00** at every rung, the break control `permute` reads **+0.23471** against
the treatment's -0.27724, and `shipped_aa2` is bit-identical to `shipped`. **I refit it myself from
the row's own published table** — exponent, intercept and r2 reproduce to all five digits, the floor
ratios to 0.01 % (display rounding on a 4-figure floor). This **supersedes the 36.9462 % /
4.763338e-02 / -0.2482 reading** and retires D136.

**The FAIL is real and the clause is NOT MET. Its margin is not currently a fact.** That
artifact sits on the `of3t-modelframe` frame, and the frame fails its own gating control at
**0.7945281613194305** against a 1e-12 bar pre-registered in commit 2520681ed — eleven orders
over, localised at pass 389 to the captured `cot_z` alone (D242). The ratio the clause computes,
0.27095922968432157 / 0.15210099830945006 = **1.7814428090278143**, is listed under CROSS-FRAME
AND THEREFORE WITHDRAWN in `of3t-frameself`'s own retraction sort. So *"compared over 99.505 %
of the mass"* is true as stated — a comparison was made for each of those parameters — but for
**5.8282 %** of it the comparison's reference sits on a frame that does not reproduce itself,
and the honest phrasing is *"compared over 99.505 %, of which 5.83 % awaits D242's repair before
the comparison means what it says"*. **The clause is deliberately not re-scored**: re-scoring on
a frame that still fails its own control would be the same defect with a newer number.

What this passage said until pass 392, and why it is worth recording rather than deleting: it
quoted `0.517117` where the artifact reads 0.27095922968432157, `3314` where it reads 3312, and
said the 5.83 % *"awaits `of3t-modelframe`"* — **a row that concluded**, having published a
clause from a frame whose gating control had not been run. "Awaits a pending row" reads as
routine work in flight; "sits on a frame that failed its own control" does not. **COVERAGE is NOT affected**: it asks
whether each loss term and conditional path FIRED (8 of 8, 11 of 11) on a real end-to-end step,
which is a question about execution and not about reference boundaries. I checked that
specifically rather than assuming D237 spread.

**It does not prove a training RUN.** Everything here is the update rule at k = 1..20. Stability
over 100k steps, precision drift, loss-scale behaviour late in training and rare sample types are
all outside it, and no amount of widening the per-step comparison reaches them. The honest sentence
is *"our training step is their training step, verified per-parameter over the mass named in
`PROVES:`, with full path coverage"* — never *"we reproduced their training run"*.

**TRAJECTORY's gate grades SHAPE, scope and coupling — not magnitude — and the magnitude is now
measured anyway.** The clause passes on shape (log-log exponent over k = 2..20 of
**-0.30639702557322707**, r2 0.9066, falling monotonically; PROTOCOL §7b fails super-linear at any
magnitude) at `rel_d` **0.22750192605686895** at k = 20. **`of3t-trajbar`'s `bar_bf16mixed_all` is
the same measurement for upstream's OWN bf16-mixed loop at the identical 761-tensor, 89.2106 %
scope**, and pass 357 scored the two against each other: **1.2707x at k = 20, never worse than
1.3677x over k = 2..20**, with the reference trajectory `d_theirs_norm` **bit-identical at all
twenty rungs**, so this is one reference and two arms rather than two experiments. That is the
magnitude statement, and it is a good one — our twenty-step trajectory sits 27 % above the
precision floor the reference itself has.

**No magnitude CLAUSE has been added to the gate, deliberately.** The number existed before any
bar could be written for it, and PROTOCOL forbids a tolerance chosen after the result. At a factor
of 1.0 the clause would fail, so adding one is not self-serving — it is simply not evidence. The
proposal belongs in PROTOCOL §9 as an amendment recording that a number already existed, and the
honest reading until then is: TRAJECTORY is MET on the three properties its clause names, and the
fourth property is measured at 1.2707x rather than graded.

**It does not prove the trunk.** 5.8282 % of the model's gradient mass is measured at 2.2341x in frame (6.402x cross-frame as published, D214) and at 6.402x
upstream's own bf16 and is the campaign's one large open accuracy object.

**Why this is not yet GO.** The clearing arm is `stackarm.py` opening the levers from a perf
script, not the training step a user runs; it is one boundary with 56 real tokens padded to

and must reproduce it by digest; `of3t-stackbound` retakes it on a real-token boundary with a
fourth exactness scope (`of3t-msafwd`'s fp32 `z` residual) for margin. If both land, exit
criterion 3 (GRADIENTS) is met on the shipped training path and the campaign can argue GO.
